precepts.text: The same pattern: take the little book and eat it up; and thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings. You have to eat, learn, and then you must go out and prophesy.
precepts.point: Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Kill: kill the old man, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Eat: devour wisdom, learn the scripture. And then go out and teach. But in that time there was no New Testament: Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Revelation says the same thing. John went to the angel and said, “Give me the little book. And he said unto me, Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.” John “took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up”, and it was sweet as honey in his mouth, and as soon as he had eaten it his belly was bitter.

Then comes the reason for the eating: “Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” The book is eaten so that it can be prophesied.

That is the same pattern as “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” You have to eat, you have to learn, and then you must go out and prophesy. John ate the book and was sent before many peoples and nations; Peter was told to eat and was sent to the house of Cornelius.

So eating in the vision means taking in the word. Rise, kill the old man, eat the word, and go out and prophesy to the scattered tribes.

precepts.text: The seventh angel's sounding marks the finishing of the mystery, when it is time to be delivered out of this place.
precepts.point: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue, and not be afraid of destruction when it comes.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” The sixth points to the sixth angel and World War II. The seventh points to completion: “But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets.”

The seventh angel's sounding marks the finishing of the mystery, when it is time to be delivered out of this place, when the Most High takes his people off the earth. In seven there shall no evil touch thee. Deliverance comes by keeping the laws and commandments, and when you fall, getting back up through fasting, praying, charity, and forgiveness of your brothers and sisters, which are heavily important in these last days.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: This is what the precept says about clouds. “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters”: not the Atlantic Ocean; it is the waters above the firmament, the third heaven. “Who maketh the clouds his chariot”: what the white man today calls unidentified flying objects.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters”: the firmament is the ozone layer. “The waters which were under the firmament”: our atmosphere. “From the waters which were above the firmament”: what we call space.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.” “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth”: that is the rainbow. This is what our sons and daughters must learn.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Write this for a memorial in a book”: a lot of times we think Moses only had two tables of stone. That’s not true; he was writing what we call today, by the Latin word biblos, the Bible.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”: Isaiah continued to write in the book.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Take thee a roll of a book, and write therein all the words that I have spoken unto thee against Israel, and against Judah”: the prophet Jeremiah continued to write the book.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “But write all things which are done in a book”: see what the angel told Tobit. The Apocrypha was always part of the Bible; it was in the Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: With the last book of the Bible: “What thou seest, write in a book.” It continued even with John; the same book Moses chronicled in, that Isaiah and Jeremiah wrote in. Today we call it the Bible, Latin for a collection of writings.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.” “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago”: he is talking about himself. Paul got stoned in the book of Acts, the disciples prayed round him, and he got back up and went back into the city to teach; that’s the level of faith. “Such an one caught up to the third heaven”: our sky is the first heaven, space where the moon is is the second, and the third heaven is where the Most High and the angels dwell. “How that he was caught up into paradise”: the proof that the third heaven is where the Most High dwells. “And heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter”: he was told it is unlawful to write that down. The Lord doesn’t want to make it so easy, because this walk is based upon faith. The scribes and Pharisees always said show us a sign; our forefathers in the wilderness with Moses saw everything, and they turned on Moses.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “But without faith it is impossible to please him”: without faith you ain’t pleasing the Lord. “And that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Paul gave us the secret to increase our faith: “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” If you spend all your time listening to Biggie Smalls or Drake, your faith is going to be very weak; if you spend your time listening to scriptures and classes, that will increase your faith, because you are feeding your spirit with the word of the Lord.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”: a lot of you ask what you need to do to endure to the end; the secret is right there. Always have a ready mind to stand fast and do the work in this truth. If you have the skill, do it, and be diligent about it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Christ told us don’t you swear. “But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool.” “Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black”: you don’t have the power to change even something as small as your hair colour, so don’t swear by anything. “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “But above all things, my brethren, swear not”: the apostle James repeated what Christ taught us. That’s why in court you can affirm instead; let your yea be yea and your nay be nay. Our forefather Jephthah swore that the first thing that came out of the door of his house he would sacrifice, and it was his little daughter.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God”: the house of God is the congregation. The Lord told Moses to take the shoes off his feet; he didn’t want Egyptian doctrine tracked up the holy mountain. Don’t track the philosophies you learned into the house of God. “And be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools”: you can’t learn if your mouth is always open. “Therefore let thy words be few.” “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it.” “Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” “Neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”: this all goes back to why Christ told us not to make vows. Angels can, because they fulfil their word.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations”: the twelve tribes fell by the sword and were led away captive. “And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: we are still living in the time of Gentile rulership, and the angel saw there should be time no longer for them to rule.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Who is the last Gentile nation to rule the earth? “What shall be the parting asunder of the times?” “Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth”: the last Gentile nation to rule the earth is Esau.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The same thing Obadiah said: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.” The last Gentile nation is Esau, and that is the kingdom we are living in right now. For you to think it’s the Arabs, Ishmael’s sons, is foolish.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Measure thou the time diligently in itself.” “Wherein the Highest will begin to visit the world which he made”: a time soon to come. “Therefore when there shall be seen earthquakes and uproars of the people in the world.” “Even so the times also of the Highest have plain beginnings in wonder and powerful works, and endings in effects and signs”: in the time of Moses there were wonders and powerful works, but in these last days people are not going to be running through the earth with power like Moses had; it is effects and signs. “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith”: you better have works in this truth. “For I have sanctified them for me from the beginning”: the elect has already been chosen, and works and faith are the evidence that you are part of the elect. “And they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments”: those that were in this truth and cast God’s laws aside and created new doctrines. “And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty”: talking about our people. “The same must know it after death by pain”: right now when people die they are at rest, as the book of Job tells you, but when Christ returns the final judgment begins. If your mama heard the truth and rejected it, she will be judged for that; this is not talking about those who never heard. “And therefore be thou not curious how the ungodly shall be punished, and when: but enquire how the righteous shall be saved, whose the world is, and for whom the world is created”: the world was created for the righteous Israelites.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Works and faith is the same thing John said: “Here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Write this down: “And I saw the seven angels which stood before God; and to them were given seven trumpets.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And the seven angels which had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The precept about the mystery of God. “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” “Among the Gentiles”: the northern kingdom of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man”: every man of Israel, not Moab, Esau, the Philistines, the Jebusites or Ishmael.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Somebody said the Bible is for everybody. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation.” “Praise ye the Lord”: we are supposed to thank God he only gave that to us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: A father leaves a will and testament to his children; it gets lost, and someone else finds it and says it’s for him. That’s how the Bible is: a will and testament to the Israelites, and when we went into slavery the nations took our writings and said this is us. “What advantage then hath the Jew?” “Chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God”: the Bible was committed to the Israelites, not to all nationalities on earth.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And thou shalt speak my words unto them”: our words must be God’s word; we must stay in the Bible. Malcolm X admitted his mistake of saying the Honourable Elijah Muhammad teaches us; that gives glory to man. People argue against a man’s point of view, but when you come with thus saith the Lord the argument ends. “For they are most rebellious”: the black man and woman, the Latin man and woman, the Native American Indian man and woman. “Open thy mouth, and eat that I give thee.” “And it was written within and without: and there was written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe”: Ezekiel saw Israel going into more and more captivities.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Eat this roll, and go speak unto the house of Israel.” “Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.” “Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them”: after he learned it, he was to speak God’s words. God’s words have power. Calling Esau a name has no power; they laugh. But when you tell them from the Bible that they are Edomites, the nation of Esau, that cuts them.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: not out of the Quran. “No one of these shall fail”: no one of these prophecies shall fail. Until you prove to me that slavery never happened to our people, according to Deuteronomy 28, 1 Kings 8, Leviticus 26 and Jeremiah 17, the Bible is a true book; our own condition proves it. “None shall want her mate”: you can’t mate the Bible with the Quran, the Gilgamesh epic or the Egyptian Book of the Dead. “For my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” This little book is enough for us. King James had 47 of the best Hebrew and Greek scholars examine the writings, and they left out the book of Enoch and the book of Jasher.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: God’s words have the power, not our own words. “Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them”: this whole thing is spiritual. God’s words burn them up on the inside, so use his words.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Eat this book. The Samaritans were the tribe of Ephraim, a small remnant that returned. “Master, eat.” “I have meat to eat that ye know not of”: the meat he is talking about is the scriptures. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work”: he compares the meat to obedience to God’s law.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: What is the will of God? “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: About bitter: “But there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness.” When you learn this book it is sweet in the beginning, then you start to see cause and effect around you, and it begins to get bitter.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Here is the sweet: “That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The kingdom is for the twelve tribes of Israel: “Which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The world is ours, more than a corner, more than Harlem: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”: some of us might be in the midst of sin, but because of what Christ did for us he will yet choose us. “And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: in obedience. “And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were”: before Christ comes back we will be in captivity under another nation’s dominion; this only fits us. “And they shall rule over their oppressors.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: How is it bitter to us as an individual? “For it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” “Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee”: your hand or foot is somebody very close to you. People ask why we cut people off; because they are an offence to this truth, and we are commanded to, however much we love them. “It is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed”: better to cast them away than for all of you to be cast into destruction.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: An easier example. “If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder”: before we had the set-up we have now, there were women who claimed to be prophetesses; one said we would be destroyed in six months, and that was 16 years ago. “For the Lord your God proveth you, to know whether ye love the Lord your God with all your heart”: in the Christian churches they say I got a word of knowledge from God for you, and it may come to pass, but its purpose is to take you away from the commandments. That is the Lord testing you. “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly”: “thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death.” This is why it gets bitter: there are people in our lives we love dearly, but we know they are wicked; some of us it is our mothers, fathers, children, husband or wife.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time”: that’s your homeboy, your home girl, your cousin who ain’t right in the spirit. Make your exit; that’s how Christ rolled. “But be continually among men of understanding.” In the beginning you might be all fired up, but after a while family says you don’t talk to us no more, you don’t come for Christmas dinner, and that begins to wear on you; now the word is bitter in your belly.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them”: have no friendship with them. Christ was among the indiscreet, but he wasn’t shooting the breeze with them; he was reproving them with the scriptures to win them to the truth. Don’t compare yourself to Christ when you’re sitting down smoking with the local drug dealer.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters”: hate means be willing to cut them off if they are keeping you from God’s law. “Yea, and his own life also”: we all had goals before we heard this gospel, some of them unlawful that would have made lots of money. Some of us are struggling now, and we think if I had taken the other road I wouldn’t be struggling like this. That’s how Satan plays with you.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful”: the lust of other things could be power or respect. When you meditate on how you could have lived compared to how you live now, it chokes the word, and the word of God becomes bitter.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: A television scene showed a so-called devout Christian woman, covetous for a house she couldn’t afford, taking a man’s money and his touch. “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms”: that’s what that touch was about. “And spend not thy money with her at the wine.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: The precept about sex. “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.” “The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.” The Zondervan Bible dictionary says marriage is an intimate personal union, consummated and continuously nourished by sexual intercourse. When marriages have problems, often there is a dry spell at home.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: When the woman in the scene was caught, rather than eat humble pie she flipped it back on her husband. “A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: When brothers say they’ll call us for counsel on what to do, that means you’ve not been studying the scripture. “And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”: the Bible commands you to escape from her. “But the sinner shall be taken by her.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the Lord”: if she steps out on you, the Bible says you cannot take her back. Wicked women look for weak brothers. Now it becomes bitter: you planned on growing old with her, you have a house and children together, and now you got to put her away because you know the law.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Two separate brothers found books of witchcraft their wives were using on them. “That maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire”: killing your children, what we call abortions today. “Or an observer of times”: horoscopes, Capricorn, Leo, Sagittarius. “Or a charmer”: lucky charms and amulets. “Or a consulter with familiar spirits”: they conjure up your dead uncle. “Or a necromancer”: somebody that talks with the dead. “For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Nebuchadnezzar deciding whether to destroy the Israelites or the Ammonites first: “For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination”: to use witchcraft. “He looked in the liver.” Nebuchadnezzar was heavy into what we call today voodoo.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep”: they see things in the future briefly. “And that mutter”: like the spirits in a Christian church with a word of knowledge. “Should not a people seek unto their God?” You women with a problem are supposed to seek the Lord, like Sarah did with Abraham, not go to Satan for a spell.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel”: witchcraft doesn’t work on us once we repent; the Lord is dealing with us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Who we learned witchcraft from: “Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines”: we learned it from the Philistines, the Hamites. “And they please themselves in the children of strangers”: another reason God cut us off.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: When our forefathers heard the gospel of Christ: “Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men”: that’s what has to happen for you to repent. You in a book of witchcraft and think God is dealing with you?

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: About people in general: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: land, singular, is Babylon the great, the United States of America. Out of this land two thirds shall be cut off and die.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Why: “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish”: with all deceit of breaking God’s law. “Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved”: two thirds of our people here will not. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie”: the white man Jesus, witchcraft and voodoo. “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” If you got a son, daughter, husband or wife like that, you got to cut them off. We are not going to make the decision for you; we read the scripture, and it is your decision whether you apply God’s law.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Habakkuk sees a vision of Christ returning and destroying Babylon the great. “They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: the nations coming against Christ. “Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: the poor are the Israelites. They will never say we hate you; they plant things among us, poison the water in Flint, Michigan, give bad education, and put abortion clinics, alcohol, drugs and guns in the communities, all done secretly. “Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters”: through great nations. “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones”: he saw so much death that he got that sick feeling. That’s what John meant: it was bitter in my belly.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Daniel said the same thing about bitterness in other words. “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”: we are going to get the world. “And all dominions shall serve and obey him.” “As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me, and my countenance changed in me”: he was glad about the earth being given to us, but he saw a lot of death and destruction coming. Like Revelation says, the blood will be up to the horses’ bridles; to witness that does something to your mind.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “In the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman”: what does the womb of a woman bring forth? Life. It is telling you from the grave the soul goes back through the woman again. We will go over that in more detail in another class.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: Here's the precept to understand what Christ meant when he said if I will that he tarry till I come. “And he said unto me,” The me is John. “Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” Meaning John would be rejuvenated, regenerated, and come back in the last days. Put that in your pipe and smoke it. People think, oh no, there's no such thing as regeneration. Hell yes it is; you're insane. When you read about John's life, he died on the island of Patmos. He didn't come again and do all of this back then. He will come again in the last days, in these last days.

points: The class is entitled the little book, sweet and bitter. “And I saw another mighty angel come down from heaven, clothed with a cloud”: it is not talking about a literal cloud of dust around him. “And a rainbow was upon his head”: the rainbow represents the covenant God made with Noah that he would never flood the earth again. It ain’t talking about same-sex marriages. Many of us see rainbows on posts and think of the LGBT; Esau takes the covenant God established and makes it something perverse. “And his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “And he had in his hand a little book open”: the little book makes reference to the Bible. “And he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left foot on the earth.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “And cried with a loud voice, as when a lion roareth”: angels didn’t talk soft either. When they spoke they had voices like lions, and this is what we got to pattern ourselves after; the Bible is meant to change us. “And when he had cried, seven thunders uttered their voices.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “I was about to write: and I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not”: we hear thunder all the time, but in the spirit John understood the language the thunder uttered. He was going to write it, and Christ said don’t write that down. The same thing was said to Paul.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “And the angel which I saw stand upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his hand to heaven”: the angel swore by the God of heaven and earth. That is something we are forbidden to do; angels can do it, but not you and I.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “That there should be time no longer”: time no longer for the Gentiles to rule this earth. The time of Gentile rule is up.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “Give me the little book”: give me that Bible. “Take it, and eat it up”: take it, study it and learn it. “And it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey”: the Lord said the same thing to Ezekiel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up”: learned it. “And it was in my mouth sweet as honey”: the sweet of the scriptures is knowing we are Israel, that Christ looks like us and is our King, that we will be saved from our enemies, that the kingdom is for us, that the world is ours, and that we will rule our oppressors. That is what draws us in. “And as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter”: the bitter of the scriptures is the results of application and knowledge, for self, friends, family and people in general. All of us are going to be tried as individuals, among friends, and in our families and marriages. It may be easy to cut off a friend or a distant family member, but it is not so easy to cut off a spouse or a child; that’s a true test of your faith. Then there is knowing that two out of every three here in America are going to be put to death.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

points: “And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings”: that lets us know John the revelator would be back in the last days; it is talking about regeneration.
